verdicts.reason: Quote states one hart and one timer; it is a configuration fact, so check=none is fine.
Quote states every register access is permitted with RACL disabled; this is exercisable by scenario accesses.

Quote states no access is rejected for access-control reasons. It is not checkable every cycle from interface signals alone, since the cause of an error response is internal. Scenario checking suffices.
Quote states the synchronous alert clocking scheme; it is a configuration fact with nothing to check, so check=none is right.

The quote 'Ping requests are never issued.' has no context. It does not name the alert channel or the condition, and the rule's wording is a restatement without a verifiable scope. Also, as a bare fragment it is ambiguous about whether it is a design property or a testbench constraint.
Quote states a single fixed configuration with no parameters to vary; it is a configuration fact with nothing to check.

duplicates.reason: Both restate the same quote: RACL disabled means all accesses are permitted and none is rejected for access-control reasons.

questions.question: Is 'Ping requests are never issued' a property of the design or a testbench/environment constraint? Which alert channel does it cover, and what is its source section?
